cohort: Pregnant women admitted with jaundice or any liver disorder to the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at Rajendra Institute of Medical Sciences, Ranchi, Jharkhand, India over a one-year period from March 2018 to February 2019.
finding: Liver dysfunction in pregnancy has a high incidence (1.52% of obstetric admissions in this study) and is associated with significant perinatal and maternal morbidity and mortality.
mod_finding: Of the 115 women with liver dysfunction admitted in labor, 75 (65.3%) had a vaginal delivery and 38 (33%) had a cesarean section.
